reading.body:
Flexential Las Vegas - Downtown in Las Vegas, Nevada, publishes 1.37 MW of IT capacity across 33,135 square feet of technical space, operated by Flexential.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 137 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 34 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Flexential Las Vegas - Downtown holds 7 published certifications: SOC 1 Type 2 (audited controls over financial reporting processes), SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), ITAR (a specific compliance or security standard), NIST 800-53 (alignment with the federal security control catalog), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Nevada has 2 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 2 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 10.37 MW. Flexential Las Vegas - Downtown contributes 1.37 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
